correctness.rationale: Stationary fourth moments exist by exponential response decay and finite fourth moments of Poisson-reset Brownian reservoirs. Conditioning on reset times makes the output a Gaussian mixture with explicit conditional variance as a sum of Brownian-increment response squares. The Poisson Mecke add-one formula and an exact gap-splitting calculation show variance nondegeneracy for every nonzero continuous signed response; a nonzero response cannot have zero insertion effect on every Poisson gap. Independence adds cumulants and a covariance-matched Gaussian OU bath has zero fourth cumulant. Exact symbolic generator and independent perpetuity checks pass, but finite examples are not used to prove the general statement.

value.rationale: A directly motivated network-wide sign theorem replaces site- and parameter-specific finite-chain kurtosis numerics: every input-coupled signed observable, including oscillatory underdamped responses, is rigorously non-Gaussian and leptokurtic. Matched Gaussian Ornstein–Uhlenbeck reservoirs have precisely identical full two-time output covariance but zero fourth cumulant, so a fourth-order measurement can distinguish reservoirs even when all second-order space-time data coincide. This is a structural and experimentally interpretable result, not an unmotivated finite special case.
